name: Baana
title: Solomon's District Governor
summary: Baana was one of King Solomon's twelve district governors responsible for supplying the king's household with food. There are several people with this name in the Bible, but the most well-known is Baana son of Ahilud, who governed the districts of Taanach and Megiddo. He played an important administrative role in Solomon's well-organized kingdom.

keyEvents.title: Appointed as District Governor
keyEvents.description: Baana son of Ahilud was appointed by King Solomon as one of twelve district governors responsible for Taanach, Megiddo and the entire Beth-shan region.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Supply System
keyEvents.description: Baana was part of Solomon's administrative system in which each governor was to supply the king's household for one month a year, reflecting the kingdom's wealth and organization.

keyEvents.title: The Kingdom of Solomon at its Height
keyEvents.description: During Solomon's reign, Judah and Israel lived in safety, and district governors like Baana ensured that the people lacked nothing.

keyEvents.title: Administration of a Strategically Important Area
keyEvents.description: Baana's district included Megiddo and Taanach, which were strategically important cities along trade routes and military roads through the Jezreel Valley.

keyEvents.title: Another Baana among those who returned from exile
keyEvents.description: A person named Baana is also mentioned among the leaders who returned from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel, showing that the name was borne by several biblical figures.
